craft_notes: Sthāyin: śānta of landing — rest, fulfillment, no-other-standing; autonomy dawning mid-proof. Feminine kept (she/her per BOUNDARY — saṃvit is she, not it; row 11 deixis). Unwon-finality disqualifies: the question demolishes by asking. Rejected: (a) neuter it → killed by BOUNDARY. (b) softening the question → killed: the question IS the demolition. Read aloud: UN-won IN-fi-nal-GROUND-ing … HOW-would-SHE-bear an-OTH-er's-GROUND.

lines: Unwon in final grounding, even by her become self-nature —
how would she bear another being's ground, its standing-place?
l4.sanskrit_cite: saivaṃ bhūtātmanā svenāpy alabdhapariniṣṭhitiḥ katham anyasya bhāvasya pratiṣṭhāspadatām iyāt

reads_against.argmap: Can the ungrounded ground another? → The unself-grounded grounds nothing: v9's inert light cannot found another being.
c1_essence: What never stood cannot stand another: consciousness fits itself to this and I, orders inert selves by double certainty, and completes severed grasping in self-rest (vv10-15).
The same self twofold — breath-bound atom, unbroken whole — gathers in one continuous end-ground where nothing shows more inert than shining (vv16-18).
